title: Theorem A: the composite lift
line: A chain of about √x theta lifts, highly divisible
summary: Theta lifts chained m times, derivatives that count primes, the seesaw identity: short lifts with small index.
story: `UpperBound` builds the chain. Source forms are lifted m times between definite hermitian spaces X₀ → X_m and restricted to Y_m: the composite lift. Its `Objects` folder defines the main objects, which much of the rest of the proof also uses. The seesaw identity (`Seesaw/SeesawIdentity`) says the lower chain applied to Poincaré series is a constant times the composite lift.

`Derivatives` supplies the divisibility: jets (Taylor coefficients) of theta functions are divisible by primes in a controlled way. The GUIDE calls them “derivatives that count primes”, and `Sharpness` shows the bound is attained. A nonzero number can’t have more prime factors than its size, so guaranteed divisibility becomes an upper bound on a sum over primes: Stepanov’s 1969 idea, done with whole numbers.
`UpperBound/Divisibility` and `UpperBound/Size` then show the composite lift is highly divisible and not too big. That is Theorem A.

modules.title: The change of directions
modules.note:
This file gives matrices over the integers of `ℂ_p`, one for each place and height, that change
given directions. For a divisor `π` of `p`, the pairings `∑ β_a ^ p ^ e * β'_a` of new directions at
a place and at its partner become divisible by `π`, apart from the exempt pairs of heights, which
involve a marked place. The valuations of the determinants, one for each column, add up to at most
the deduction: `v(π)` times the sum of the numbers `New.deductionTerm`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.deductionTerm`: the term of the deduction for a place, a partner and an exponent `e`.
* `New.CongruenceChoice`, `New.exists_congruenceChoice_cost_eq_and_covers`: which congruences are
  imposed for a place and a partner; a choice of cost `New.deductionTerm` covers the pairs of
  heights that are not exempt (`New.IsExemptPair`).
* `New.newDirection`, `New.exists_newDirection_dvd`: integral changes of direction at each place
  and height that make the pairings that are not exempt divisible by `π`, and whose determinants
  cost at most the deduction.

Notions from other files:
* `New.valRingCp p`: the integers of `ℂ_p`.

modules.title: Couplings and the normal form
modules.note:
* `New.coupling`, `New.couplingSum`, `New.HasNormalForm`: the couplings `Γ_e` and the normal form
  `F(ϖ z) = W exp (c_ϖ Ξ)` with `W` integral, `c_ϖ = ϖ ^ (p + 1) / p` and
  `Ξ = ∑_{e ∈ S} ∑_j λ_{e j} Γ_e ^ p ^ j`, for any rule that assigns partners to places.
* `New.HasNormalForm.rescale`: the normal form is kept, with other numbers `λ_{e j}`, under
  `z ↦ α z` with `α` integral; so its existence depends only on the valuation of `ϖ`
  (`New.HasNormalForm.exists_of_norm_eq`).
* `New.HasNormalForm.norm_coeff_subst_le_one`: if `F` has the normal form and `Z` is integral
  without constant term, then `F(ϖ Z)` is integral in degrees at most `B` if the couplings `Γ_e(Z)`
  with `e ∈ S`, `e ≤ log_p B` are divisible by some `π` with `‖c_ϖ π‖ ≤ p ^ (-1 / (p - 1))`.
* `New.HasNormalForm.of_dvd_sub`: it is enough to know the exponent modulo such a `π`.
* `New.dvd_pderiv_couplingSum_sub`: the derivatives of `Ξ` modulo `p`, if `0 ∉ S`. They are not
  needed for the divisibility bound, only for its sharpness.

## Notation

* `valRingCp p` is the valuation ring `𝒪` of `ℂ_[p]`; a series over it is called integral.
* `seriesToCp W` is the series `W` over `𝒪`, seen as a series over `ℂ_[p]`.
* `expSubst g` is the series `exp g`, for `g` without constant term.
* The variables `z_x` are indexed by pairs `x = (τ, i)` in `Φ × c`, for finite types `Φ` and `c`;
  the elements `τ` of `Φ` are called places.

modules.title: Divisibility of the jets of a series with the normal form along products of minors
modules.note:
* `New.norm_jet_le_of_isHomogeneous`: Legendre's bound for the jet of an integral series along a
  homogeneous integral polynomial.
* `New.minorProd`, `New.predictedDivisibility`: products of minors, and the divisibility predicted
  by their shape.
* `New.Parameters.norm_jet_minorProd_le_of_hasNormalForm`: the count. The jet of a series with the
  normal form along a product of minors has the predicted divisibility, up to an error term.
* `New.Parameters.norm_jet_minorProd_le_of_charges`: the count with charges. The columns of height
  one at a set of marked places are removed from the prediction, and powers `p ^ w` of `p` on the
  rows, the charges, pay for them. The exponents `w` satisfy the condition of `New.IsChargeExponent`
  for pairs of columns that occur in `κ`, and `New.fillingCharge` is their sum over the boxes.
* `New.exists_norm_schurJet_le_norm_jet_minorProd`: an entry of the Schur matrix may be replaced by
  a product of minors of `z y` with `y` integral.

A linear substitution makes the couplings that matter in the degree of the jet divisible by `π_p`,
so that the series becomes integral in that degree. Legendre's bound applies, and the chain rule
gives the factor whose valuation is deducted. Each box gains about `γ_p`, and the deduction is
`v(π_p)` times a sum of numbers `New.deductionTerm`. The argument is carried out once, with charges
(`New.Parameters.norm_jet_minorProd_le_of_isChargeExponent`); the count itself is the case without
marked places and with all charges equal to one.

Notions from other files:
* `valRingCp p`: the valuation ring of `ℂ_[p]`; its elements are called integral, and a lower bound
  for a valuation is written as an upper bound for the norm.
* `New.jet R Q F`: the number `(Q(∂) F)(0)`, for a polynomial `Q` and a power series `F`.
* `New.WeylIndex n κ`, `New.schur`, `New.schurJet`: `κ τ h` is the number of columns of height `h`
  of a diagram at the place `τ`. The standard fillings of these diagrams index the Schur matrix of a
  family of matrices `z_τ`, and `schurJet κ F` is the matrix of jets of `F` along its entries.
* `New.coupling pr e`: the series `Γ_e = ∑ z_(τ, c) ^ p ^ e * z_(pr e τ, c)`, where `pr e τ` is the
  partner of the place `τ`. `New.deductionTerm p κ N marked τ τ' e` is the real number
  `min (t / p ^ e) (r' + t') + r / p ^ e + min (B / p ^ e) B'`. Only heights below `N` count: `t`
  is the number of columns of height one at `τ` (zero if `τ ∈ marked`), `r` that of the low columns
  (the other ones) and `B` that of their boxes. The primed letters refer to `τ'`.
* For `K = ℚ(√-d)`: `χ_K = New.chiK d`, `π_p = New.piPrimeInt d` has valuation
  `v(π_p) = New.piPrimeValuation d p`, `ρ_p = New.varpiValuation d p`, and
  `γ_p = New.gammaPrime d p = 1 / (p - 1) - ρ_p`. The set `I_p° = New.partnerExponents d p` consists
  of the odd numbers if `p` is inert and of all numbers if `p = d`, and
  `I_p = New.positivePartnerExponents d p` of its positive elements. `New.Parameters.partner` is the
  partner `-p ^ e τ` of `τ`.
* `New.HasNormalForm`: `F(ϖ z)` is an integral series times the exponential of `ϖ ^ (p + 1) / p`
  times an integral combination of the powers `Γ_e ^ p ^ j`.

modules.title: Different and prime decomposition of the CM field E = K(ζ)
modules.note:
Let `K = ℚ(√-d) ⊆ ℂ` and `E = P.E s = K(ζ)`, with `ζ` a primitive root of unity of order `q₁`.
`star` is complex conjugation on `E`. This file computes the different of `E`, gives it a purely
imaginary generator, and describes how the primes `p ∤ q₁ d` decompose in `E`. The infinite
places `v` of `E` form a group isomorphic to `Gal(E/K)` and to `(ℤ/q₁)ˣ`, and `v • w` is the
pullback of a finite place `w` along the automorphism `P.galOfPlace s v`. In the comments P'(ζ)
stands for `New.Parameters.relDifferentGen`, the value at `ζ` of the derivative of the cyclotomic
polynomial of order `q₁`; this letter P is not the parameters.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Parameters.deltaE`, `New.Parameters.star_deltaE`,
  `New.Parameters.differentIdeal_eq_span_deltaE`: the imaginary generator of the different of `E`.
* `New.Parameters.smul_eq_iff_exists_frobElem_pow`: for a prime `p ∤ q₁ d` and `w` above `p`, the
  place `v` sends `w` to `w` exactly when `(v, 1)` is a power of the Frobenius element
  `New.Parameters.frobElem` in the monoid `P.Φ s × ℤ`, and to `w̄` exactly when `(v, -1)` is. For
  such `p`, `New.Parameters.q_eq_pow_orderOf_frobElem` gives the norm of `w`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters`: a multiple `q₀` of `18480 = 16 · 3 · 5 · 7 · 11` and a prime `d` with
  `d ≡ q₀/2 - 1 mod q₀`.
* `New.Parameters.q₁`: the number `q₁ = 3 ^ c * 2 ^ s * q₀`, with `c = ⌊log₃ s⌋ + 5`.
* `New.Parameters.Φ`: `P.Φ s` is the group of infinite places of `E`. It is distinct from the bare
  `Φ` of the CM type of `E` (`New.CMType`): `Φ v : E →+* ℂ` is the embedding over `K` inducing `v`.

modules.title: Weil data of the CM field E = K(ζ) and the number s₀
modules.note:
Let `K = ℚ(√-d) ⊆ ℂ` and `E = P.E s = K(ζ)`, with `ζ` a primitive root of unity of order `q₁`;
`star` is complex conjugation on `E`. The infinite places `v` of `E` form a group isomorphic to
`Gal(E/K)` and to `(ℤ/q₁)ˣ`, and `v • w` is the pullback of a finite place `w` along the
automorphism `P.galOfPlace s v`. This file describes the places of `E` above a prime
`p ≡ 1` mod `q₁ d` and builds the Weil data of `E`. From the idele α of these data it defines the
number s₀ = `New.Parameters.vacuumRoot`, a root of `(chiFin α)⁻¹`, and computes the absolute
values of its conjugates over `K`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Parameters.q_eq_of_modEq_one`, `New.Parameters.nonempty_infinitePlace_equiv_finPlace`: for
  `p ≡ 1` mod `q₁ d` the places above `p` have norm `p`. If `a ∈ 𝓞 E` has `a ā = p c` with `c : ℕ`
  prime to `p`, those that divide `a` are in bijection with the infinite places.
* `New.Parameters.α`: the idele with component 1/P'(ζ) at the places that divide
  `New.Parameters.betaKInE` and 1 elsewhere.
* `New.Parameters.instWeilDataE`: the Weil data, with ȷ = −1/√−d.
* `New.Parameters.norm_gal_vacuumRoot`: for every automorphism `σ` of `ℂ` over `K`, ‖σ s₀‖ ^ 2 is
  the root discriminant of `E` divided by `√d`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters`: a multiple `q₀` of `18480 = 16 · 3 · 5 · 7 · 11` and a prime `d` with
  `d ≡ q₀/2 - 1 mod q₀`; `New.Parameters.q₁` is `3 ^ c * 2 ^ s * q₀`, with `c = ⌊log₃ s⌋ + 5`.
* `New.Parameters.Φ`: `P.Φ s` is the group of infinite places of `E`. It is distinct from the bare
  `Φ` of the CM type of `E` (`New.CMType`): `Φ v : E →+* ℂ` is the embedding over `K` inducing `v`.
* `New.WeilData`: an imaginary element ȷ, a finite idele α and a splitting character υ.
* `New.chiFin`: the character x ↦ υ(x)|x|^(−1/2) of the finite ideles of `E`, x being extended by
  1 at infinity.
* `New.Parameters.relDifferentGen`: P'(ζ), the value at `ζ` of the derivative of the cyclotomic
  polynomial of order `q₁`; it generates the different of `E/K`.

modules.title: Chosen places, characters of given weight, finiteness of pairs and sizes of the different
modules.note:
Fix admissible data `D` (`New.Data`) with primes p₀, p₁ (p_i is `D.levelPrime i`) and an integer
`D.piMBar` of K of norm p₀p₁. The chosen places are the finite places of E that divide the complex
conjugate of `D.piMBar`.

The file defines residue characters at the chosen places, characters of U(1)(𝔸) of given weight and
pairs, and proves that there are finitely many pairs. It also bounds the generator of the different
of E and the root discriminant at the infinite places between `x ^ 10` and `x ^ 12`, where `log x`
is `D.logX`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.IsChosen`, `New.Data.ChosenPlace`: the chosen places, and those above p_i. Each lies
  above p₀ or p₁ (`New.Data.exists_levelPrime_mem_of_isChosen`). A place above p_i has norm p_i
  (`New.Data.q_eq_levelPrime`).
* `New.Data.chiMLocal`: residue characters of order q₂ at the chosen places, trivial elsewhere. At a
  chosen place it is the q₂-th power of a character `New.Data.chiMLocalRoot` of order q₂².
* `New.Data.chiZero`, `New.Data.chiM`: characters of U(1)(𝔸) of weight -w₀ and trivial tame part,
  and of weight 0 and tame part `New.Data.chiMLocal`. By
  `New.AutChar.exists_hasWeight_of_prod_eq_one` they exist because the formula of
  `New.AutChar.HasWeight` gives 1 on the integral rational points of U(1), which are q₁-th roots of
  unity (`New.Data.exists_char_hasWeight`).
* `New.Data.CriticalPair`: a character of weight -c with tame part trivial off the chosen places,
  and an integer z with 1 ≤ z ≤ t and z ≤ c ≤ 4b. There are finitely many
  (`New.Data.finite_criticalPair`).
* `New.Data.hasLogBound_deltaE`: at every infinite place the generator `New.Parameters.deltaE` of
  the different has absolute value in `[x ^ 10, x ^ 12]`.
* `New.Data.rootDisc_mem_Icc`, `New.Data.hasLogBound_rootDisc`: so does the root discriminant
  `New.Data.rootDisc`, their geometric mean. The class `D.HasLogBound u F l` says `|F| ≤ exp l` for
  `u = true` and `exp l ≤ F` for `u = false`; so `(if u then 12 else 10) * log x` gives both bounds
  at once.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.E`: The field E = K(ζ), ζ a primitive root of unity of order q₁, a multiple of q₀ that
  depends on the exponent s = `D.towerExp` of the data; `New.Data.Φ` is the type of its infinite
  places.
* `New.AutChar`: The group of continuous circle-valued characters of U(1)(𝔸), the norm-one adeles of
  the CM field E, trivial on elements coming from E.
* `New.AutChar.HasWeight`: μ has weight e and tame part ψ: almost all residue characters ψ_w are
  trivial, and μ(u) = ∏_v u_v^{e(v)} · ∏_w ψ_w(u mod w) whenever u has integral finite part.
* `New.Parameters.q₂`: The natural number q₂ = (q₀d)^(s+6); q₂² divides p_i - 1.
* `New.Data.liftWeight`: The number w_j(σ) = κ(σ) + (j + 1/2) Δ, with κ = `New.Data.weight`, the gap
  Δ = `New.Data.gap` and Δ/2 = `New.Data.halfGap`.

modules.title: Frobenius congruence for `θ` and the coefficient of `z ^ (p - 1)` in `x`
modules.group: The formal group and the exponential factor
modules.note:
Let `d ≡ 7` modulo `8` be a prime, `C` a lattice with complex multiplication by the integers of
`K = ℚ(√-d)`, and `p` a prime that does not split in `K`. This file proves that
`θ(π_p z) / θ(z) ^ q_p` is `1` modulo `π_p` in `𝒪[[y]]`. For `g = -log θ` it follows that
`q_p g(z) - g(π_p z)` lies in `π_p 𝒪[[y]]`. Independently of this congruence, it shows by a
recursion that at an inert prime the coefficient of `z ^ (p - 1)` in `x` is a unit; this is used in
the last step for the exponent on one curve (`New.CMLattice.norm_coeff_exponentSeries_eq_one`).

Notions from other files:
* `chiK d p` is the Legendre symbol `(p / d)`: it is `1`, `-1`, `0` when `p` is split, inert,
  ramified in `K`.
* `π_p = piPrime d p` is `√-d` for `p = d` and `p` otherwise; `q_p = primeNorm d p` is `p ^ 2` for
  inert `p` and `p` otherwise.
* `PadicPlace p` is the choice of a ring homomorphism `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]`, and `taylorVia ιₚ f` is
  the Taylor series of `f` at `0`, with coefficients sent to `ℂ_[p]` by `ιₚ`.
* `θ`, `x`, `y` are the series of the theta function `C.θ`, of `C.translatedX z = ℘(z + t) - ℘(t)`
  and of `C.translatedY z = (℘'(z + t) - a₁ x(z)) / 2`. Here `t = C.t` is the chosen point of order
  two, the lattice is scaled so that `℘''(t) = 2`, and `a₁ = C.a₁` satisfies `a₁ ^ 2 = 12 ℘(t)`;
  moreover `g = C.negLogTheta = -log θ`.
* `C.integralSeriesRing = 𝒪[[y]]` is the ring of power series in `y` with coefficients in the
  valuation ring `𝒪` of `ℂ_[p]`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.CMLattice.exists_rescale_theta_eq_pow_mul_one_add_smul`: at a non-split prime `p` the
  quotient `θ(π_p z) / θ(z) ^ q_p` is `1` modulo `π_p` in `𝒪[[y]]`.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_negLogTheta_frobenius_congruence`: `q_p g(z) - g(π_p z) ∈ π_p 𝒪[[y]]` for
  `g = -log θ`.
* `New.CMLattice.norm_coeff_taylorVia_translatedX_eq_one`: at an inert prime `p` the coefficient
  of `z ^ (p - 1)` in the series `x` is a unit.

modules.title: The exponent on one curve
modules.group: The formal group and the exponential factor
modules.note:
Let `d ≡ 7` mod `8` be a prime (`PrimeSevenModEight d`), let `p` be a prime that does not split in
`ℚ(√-d)`, and let `𝒪` (`valRingCp p`) be the ring of integers of `ℂ_p`; a series is integral if its
coefficients lie in `𝒪`.

* `New.CMLattice.exists_exponent_tsum`: for some `ϖ` of valuation `ρ_p` the series `θ(ϖ z)` is
  integral up to one exponential `exp (c_ϖ Ξ₁)`, where `c_ϖ = ϖ ^ (p + 1) / p`, the series `Ξ₁` is
  integral, and modulo `π_p` it has only terms `(z ^ p ^ e * z) ^ p ^ j` with `e ∈ I_p°`
  (`partnerExponents d p`: the odd numbers, and all numbers if `p = d`).

The proof has four steps.

1. Averaging `ζ ^ (-p - 1) g(ζ z)` over the `(q_p - 1)`-th roots of unity `ζ` replaces `g = -log θ`
   by its part `g^♭` in the degrees `≡ p + 1` mod `q_p - 1`.
2. The Frobenius congruence gives a functional equation for `Ξ₁ = -g^♭(ϖ z) / c_ϖ`.
3. The equation is solved degree by degree. With `Y = T(ϖ z) / ϖ ≡ ∑_j z ^ q_p ^ j` and a number
   `λ ∈ 𝒪` one has `Ξ₁ ≡ λ Y ^ (p + 1)` for inert `p` and `Ξ₁ ≡ λ (Y ^ 2 - z ^ 2 / 2)` for `p = d`.
   The coefficients of the terms are `λ` in the first case, and `λ / 2`, `λ` or `2 λ` in the second.
4. For inert `p` the coefficient of `z ^ (p + 1)` in `Ξ₁` is a unit, and so is `λ`.

Notions from other files:
* `chiK d p` is the Legendre symbol `(p / d)`; the prime `p` is non-split if `chiK d p ≠ 1`.
* `q_p = primeNorm d p` is the norm of a prime above `p`, `π_p = piPrime d p` is `√-d` if `p = d`
  and `p` otherwise, and `ρ_p = varpiValuation d p` is `v(π_p) / (q_p - 1)` with `v(p) = 1`.
* `C : CMLattice d` is a lattice in `ℂ` that is stable under the ring of integers of `ℚ(√-d)`, with
  a chosen point `t` of order two.
* `taylorVia ιₚ C.θ` is the Taylor series over `ℂ_p` of the theta function `θ` of `C`, along the
  embedding `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]` fixed by `PadicPlace p`, and `C.negLogTheta` is `g = -log θ`.
* `C.integralSeriesRing` is the ring `𝒪[[y]] = 𝒪[[T]]`, where `y` is the Taylor series of
  `C.translatedY` and `T = C.formalParam` is the formal parameter.

modules.title: Resolutions of the identity and power series in the compositions `y(μ_i z)`
modules.group: The formal group and the exponential factor
modules.note:
This file is about families of vectors `u j` in `Eⁿ`, taken `m j` times, with
`z = ∑ m j (u j† z) u j` for all complex vectors `z` indexed by `InfinitePlace E × n`, where `u j`
is read as such a vector through the CM type, and about power series composed with linear forms
`μ_i z`: products of the series `θ(μ_i z)`, for the theta function `θ` of a lattice `C`, and
integral series in the `y(μ_i z)`, for the parameter `y` of the elliptic curve of `C`.

The following imported notions occur in the statements.

* `Φ w` is the complex embedding of the CM type at the infinite place `w` of `E`.
* `ιₚ` is a fixed embedding of `ℂ` into `ℂ_p`, and `valRingCp p` is the closed unit ball of `ℂ_p`.
* `C.multiSeriesRing μ` is the ring of power series with integral coefficients in the series
  `y(μ_i z)`, where `y` is the Taylor series of the parameter `C.translatedY` of the curve.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.dagger`: the coefficients of the linear form `y† z` of a vector `y` in `Eⁿ`;
  `New.daggerForms`: the same for a family of vectors, read in `ℂ_p`.
* `New.IsResolution`: families of vectors `u j`, taken `m j` times, with
  `z = ∑ m j (u j† z) u j` (Parseval frames).
* `New.IsIntegralAbove`: elements of `E` that are integral at all places above `p`; they are
  quotients of elements of `𝓞 E` by natural numbers prime to `p`
  (`New.IsIntegralAbove.exists_mul_eq`).
* `New.CMLattice.thetaProd`: the product of copies of `θ` along linear forms.
* `New.CMLattice.rescale_thetaProd`, `New.CMLattice.rescale_mem_multiSeriesRing`: scaling the
  variables scales the linear forms in a product of copies of `θ` and in an integral series in
  copies of the parameter.
* `New.CMLattice.pderiv_mem_multiSeriesRing`: for integral linear forms, partial derivatives
  preserve the ring of such series.

modules.title: The normal form of theta products at non-split primes
modules.group: The formal group and the exponential factor
modules.note:
The file treats products of theta functions at a prime `p` that is not split in `K = ℚ(√-d)`. Here
`θ` is the theta function of the CM curve, `y` the parameter `C.translatedY` of the curve, composed
with the forms `u† z`, and `E` is `K` with a root of unity adjoined.

The vectors `u` of `Eⁿ` form a resolution of the identity and are integral above `p`. The partner of
an infinite place `τ` of `E` is `-p ^ e τ`, and `Γ_e` is the coupling of the places with their
partners. Congruences modulo `π_p` between powers at a place and conjugation at its partner lead to
a normal form for `∏ θ(u_j† z) ^ m j` times an integral series in the `y(u† z)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Parameters.norm_pow_sub_conj_partner_le`: for `e` in `I_p°`, modulo `π_p`, the `p ^ e`-th
  power at a place `τ` is complex conjugation at its partner `-p ^ e τ`.
* `New.Parameters.piPrimeInt_dvd_sum_linearSeries_sub_coupling`: at a non-split `p`, for a
  resolution of the identity by vectors `u` integral above `p`, the sum
  `∑ m j * (u_j† z) ^ p ^ e * (u_j† z)` is the coupling `Γ_e` modulo `π_p` for `e` in `I_p°`.
* `New.Parameters.exists_hasNormalForm`: at a non-split prime `p`, for a resolution of the identity
  by vectors `u` integral above `p`, the product `∏ θ(u_j† z) ^ m j` times an integral series in the
  `y(u† z)` has the normal form.

Notions from other files:
* `New.piPrime`, `New.piPrimeInt`: the number `π_p`, which is `√-d` if `p = d` and `p` otherwise, in

* `New.chiK`, `New.partnerExponents`: the character `χ_K`, with `χ_K(p) ≠ 1` at non-split `p`, and

* `New.IsResolution`: the vectors `u` with multiplicities `m` satisfy `z = ∑ m j (u_j† z) u_j`,

* `New.coupling`, `New.HasNormalForm`: `Γ_e = ∑ z_(τ,c) ^ p ^ e * z_(τ',c)` with `τ'` the partner

modules.title: Scale of theta Taylor series, tight frames, jet series along lines
modules.note:
Let `P` be parameters, `d = P.d` and `K = ℚ(i√d)`. The file fixes the scale at which Taylor series
of theta functions are taken, and it builds theta functions from tight frames. For a space `V` with
all signs `1` and `f` in `New.Space.finitePart`, the function `New.Space.entireTheta f` is entire on
`ℂ^(places × n)`. A tight frame of length `M` is a finite family of vectors `y` of the lattice `𝔞₀`,
counted with multiplicities, such that `∑ y, (y† z) y = M z` for all `z` in `ℂ^places`, where `y`
stands for the vector of its images `τ y` under the CM type and `y† z = ∑ τ, conj (τ y) * z τ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Parameters.areaScale` is `√(2π / √d)`, and `New.Parameters.periodFactor` is `vacuumRoot`
  divided by the unit of `New.CMLattice.chowla_selberg`.
* `New.Parameters.jetScale`: the scale `periodFactor * areaScale / cmPeriod`.
* `New.Parameters.isTightFrame_pow`: the powers of a primitive `q₁`-th root of unity are a tight
  frame of length `q₁`.
* `New.Space.taylor_line_eq_subst_jetSeries`: the Taylor series of `z ↦ entireTheta f (a • z)` on
  the line spanned by a vector `v` is the restriction of `jetSeries V a f`.
* `New.Parameters.IsResolutionProduct`: the theta functions of the rational translates of a vector
  are products of translated entire functions of linear forms; `IsResolutionProduct.theta_translate`
  and `IsResolutionProduct.jetSeries_translate` give their theta values and Taylor series.
* `New.Parameters.exists_isResolutionProduct_of_isTightFrame`: a product of monomial sections,
  pulled back along a tight frame, is the theta function of a vector with integral values.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters`: a multiple `q₀` of `18480 = 16 · 3 · 5 · 7 · 11` and a prime `d` with
  `d ≡ q₀/2 - 1 mod q₀`. The CM field `E = P.E s` is generated over `K` by a primitive `q₁`-th root
  of unity `ζ`, `q₁ = P.q₁ s`, and `Φ τ : E →+* ℂ` is the embedding of its CM type at the infinite
  place `τ`.
* `New.finiteImage`: for a family `γ` in `E`, the finite adeles `α⁻¹ γ k`, with `α = P.α s` the
  idele of the fractional ideal `𝔞₀`; so `finiteImage id y ∈ Ô E` says that `y` lies in
  `𝔞₀ = E ∩ α Ô`.
* `New.PadicPlace`: a `p`-adic place of `ℂ`, that is, a ring homomorphism `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]`.
* `New.Space.entireTheta`: for `f` in the space `𝒮 V` of a hermitian space `V`, the function
  `y ↦ θ(ϱ(y) f) exp(|y|²/2)` of a real vector `y` in Fock coordinates, with `θ` the theta
  functional `V.θ` and `ϱ` the Heisenberg representation `V.ϱ`.
* `finVec x`: the adelic vector with finite part `α x` and real part zero. So
  `V.ϱ (finVec (finiteImage γ)) f` is the translate of `f` by the finite image of `γ`.
* `New.CMLattice`: a lattice `C.Λ` in `ℂ`, stable under the integers of `K`, with a marked point of
  order two. Its hermitian form is `C.hermitianForm l z = (π / A) * conj l * z`, with `A = C.area`
  the area of a period parallelogram, and `C.twistedTranslate m l g` is the translate
  `z ↦ g (z + l)` times the Gaussian factor of the form `m • C.hermitianForm`. A section of degree
  `m` is multiplied by `C.multiplier l ^ m` under this translation for `l` in `C.Λ`, where
  `C.multiplier l` is a number of absolute value one.
* `pullForm φ B`: the pull-back `(u, v) ↦ B (φ u) (φ v)` of a form along a linear map `φ`.
* `New.Space.jetSeries`: the series whose coefficient of `z ^ k` is `a ^ |k| / k!` times the theta
  functional of `v ⊗ f`, where `v` is the Fock vector of the monomial `z ^ k`.
modules.literature:
A product of monomial sections of a CM curve, pulled back along a tight frame at scale `a / δ̄`, for
an integer `δ` of `K` and a point `a` of the lattice of the curve, is the theta function of a vector
of the finite part, by Fourier inversion. The theta value and the jet series of each rational
translate are the products of those of the translated sections. The values of the vector are
products of torsion values of monomials, so they are integral at every `p`-adic place. Eutactic
stars (sets of vectors that form a tight frame), the isogeny formula for theta functions and
integrality via torsion values are known from the literature. Related work: Conway–Sloane,
Low-dimensional lattices V, 1989; Finis, Divisibility of anticyclotomic L-functions and theta
functions with CM, 2006; Mumford, On the equations defining abelian varieties I, 1966.

modules.title: The integral vacuum θ°: integrality and bounds of its values, standard data at p
modules.note:
Fix the parameters `P`, the field `E = P.E s` and a hermitian space `V` of rank `n` over it. The
integral vacuum θ° = `New.Parameters.intVacuum` is the vacuum scaled by `vacuumScale ^ n`. The
factor `New.Parameters.vacuumScale` is provided by
`New.Parameters.exists_mul_vacElem_integral_bounded` for the standard space of rank one. To obtain
it, a multiple of the vacuum is written as a sum of translates of one vector. For a standard space,
the values of θ° at the points `New.finVec x` are integral at every prime, have bounded conjugates,
and are not all zero. A vector `f` is read as the function `f y = θ(ϱ(y) f)` of adelic vectors `y`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Parameters.IsThetaProduct`, `New.Parameters.exists_isThetaProduct`: a vector whose theta
  function is the product of theta functions of a CM lattice along the resolution of powers of `ζ`,
  that is, along the vectors `ζᵏ / q₁`, `k < q₁`, which form a tight frame of `E` over `K`.
* `New.Parameters.standardData V δ`: the module of standard data at a prime `p`. Its scalars are the
  complex numbers that the `p`-adic place sends to integers, and it is spanned by the translates
  `V.finHeisenbergOp x θ°`, for the `x` with `δ x` integral above `p`.
* `New.Parameters.norm_intVacuum_le_one`: the values of θ° at the points `New.finVec x` are integral
  at every prime.
* `New.Parameters.norm_ringEquiv_intVacuum_le`: their conjugates under the automorphisms of `ℂ` are
  bounded; `New.Parameters.norm_gal_intVacuum_le` is the case of automorphisms over `K`.
* `New.Parameters.norm_dataInner_self_le`: a bound for `f` at these points bounds its squared norm
  `New.Space.dataInner f f`, the mean of `|f y| ^ 2` over adelic vectors modulo rational ones.
* `New.Parameters.exists_isJetConjugate_translates`: the conjugates of the jets of the translates of
  one vector that generates the finite part.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters`: The fixed parameters: a multiple `q₀` of `18480 = 16 · 3 · 5 · 7 · 11` and a
  prime `d` with `d ≡ q₀/2 - 1 mod q₀`.
* `New.Parameters.E`: The field E = K(ζ) obtained from K = ℚ(√-d) by adjoining a primitive root of
  unity ζ of order `P.q₁ s`.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.vacElem`: The vacuum: the product of the Gaussian and a twisted indicator of a lattice,
  as an element of 𝒮(V).
* `New.Space.IsStd`: The space `V` is standard: all its signs are `+1` and its point is the identity
  matrix.

modules.title: Integrality of jets of theta products and stability of standard data
modules.note:
This file proves two facts. Let `μ_i` be linear forms that are `d` times integral forms, and let `y`
be the parameter described below. Then the derivatives at `0` of a product of series `θ(μ_i z)`,
times an integral series in the `y(μ_i z)`, are integral.
Standard data of level `δ` are stable under the Heisenberg operators of finite points that `δ`
makes integral above `p`, and under the Weil operators of finite points that are integral above
`p`. An element of `ℂ_[p]` is integral if its norm is at most `1`.

* `New.jet`: the pairing `(Q(∂) F)(0)` of a polynomial `Q` with a power series `F`.
* `New.taylorVia ιₚ C.θ`: the Taylor series at `0` of the function `θ` of the CM lattice `C`, with
  coefficients sent to `ℂ_[p]` by `ιₚ`; and `New.linearSeries c`, the linear form `∑ c_x z_x`.
* `New.CMLattice.multiSeriesRing`: the integral power series in the `y(μ_i z)`, where the parameter
  `y` is the Taylor series of `C.translatedY`.
* `New.Parameters.integralAfter δ S`: the finite adelic vectors `x` with `δ x` integral at the
  places in `S`.
* `New.Parameters.standardData V δ`: the module over `New.embValRing` spanned by the translates of
  the integral vacuum by the points that `δ` makes integral above `p`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.CMLattice.jetRing`: the ring generated by the integral series in the `y(μ_i z)` and by the
  `θ(μ_i z)` and `(-log θ)'(μ_i z)`.
* `New.Parameters.finHeisenbergOp_mem_standardData`: standard data of level `δ` are stable under the
  Heisenberg operators of finite points that `δ` makes integral above `p`.
* `New.Parameters.omega_mem_standardData`: they are stable under the Weil operators of finite
  points integral above `p`.

modules.title: The scale of the Taylor series of a vector
modules.note:
* `New.Space.jet_jetSeries_of_isHomogeneous`: the derivative of the Taylor series along a
  homogeneous polynomial is a theta value times a power of the scale.
* `New.Parameters.norm_periodFactor_mul_daggerForms_le_one`: the scaled linear form of a vector `y`
  is integral at `p` if `α⁻¹ y` is integral above `p`.
* `New.Parameters.norm_jetScale_sq`: the modulus of `jetScale`, from the area of the CM lattice and
  the formula of Chowla and Selberg.

The period scale is `jetScale` times an integer `π_M` of `K` of norm `M`. The statements with this
factor are `New.Data.norm_conj_piMBar_mul_jetScale_sq` and
`New.Data.norm_taylorScale_eq_one_of_not_dvd`.

The statements use these notions:
* `jetSeries a f`: the Taylor series of the theta function of `f`, with variables scaled by `a`;
  `jet R Q F` is the derivative at zero of the series `F` along the polynomial `Q`.
* `daggerForms u j`: the coefficients in `ℂ_p` of the linear form `z ↦ y† z` of the vector
  `y = u j`; at a pair `(v, i)` of an infinite place and a coordinate the coefficient is the image
  in `ℂ_p` of the complex conjugate of `Φ_v (y i)`, with `Φ_v` the embedding chosen at `v`.
* `periodFactor`: the complex number `vacuumRoot / chowlaSelbergUnit`, where `vacuumRoot` is a root
  of the inverse of the value `chiFin α` of a character at the idele `α` and the denominator is a
  unit at every `p`-adic place; `jetScale` is `periodFactor * √(2π / √d) / cmPeriod`, where
  `cmPeriod * 𝓞_K` is the lattice of the CM curve of the field `K = ℚ(i√d)`.
modules.literature:
The modulus of `jetScale` is computed from the formula of Chowla and Selberg,
`New.CMLattice.chowla_selberg`.

modules.title: Tight frames in `𝔞₀`
modules.note:
A tight frame of length `h` is a finite family of vectors `y` of the lattice `𝔞₀`, counted with
multiplicities, such that `∑ y, (y† z) y = h z` for all `z`: a resolution of `h`.

* `New.Parameters.exists_isTightFrame_coprime`: a tight frame in `𝔞₀` of a length `h` prime to `q₁`,
  namely `New.Parameters.dualResolutionFactor`.
* `New.Parameters.exists_isTightFrame_of_coprime`: this frame and the powers of `ζ` give tight
  frames of every length `m ≥ q₁ h + R (q₁ + h)` with multiplicities at least `R`.
* `New.Data.exists_short_isTightFrame_coprime`: the length `h` is at most the weight `b`, and the
  two frames contain a vector `y` with `HasUnitLinearForm`.
* `New.Data.exists_isTightFrame`: a tight frame of length `p₀ p₁ = D.M` with large multiplicities,
  where `p₀` and `p₁` are the two primes `D.levelPrime 0` and `D.levelPrime 1` of the data.

The powers of `ζ` are a tight frame of length `q₁`. The frame of length `h` comes from the powers of
`ζ⁻¹` and the orbits `ζ ^ k * τ(e i)` of a multiple `e i` in `𝔞₀` of their dual basis for the
Hermitian form `y'† y`, by replacing some pairs of members by their sums; the cross terms add
`β ^ j + conj β ^ j` to the length, which makes it prime to `q₁`.

Notions from other files:
* `P.E s` is the field `E = K(ζ)`, where `K = ℚ(√-d)` and `ζ = P.ζ s` is a primitive root of unity
  of order `q₁ = P.q₁ s = P.q₀ * towerDeg s`; here `q₀ = P.q₀` is the fixed modulus of the
  parameters and `towerDeg s = 3 ^ (log₃ s + 5) * 2 ^ s`. `P.zetaInt s` is `ζ` as an element of
  `𝓞 E`. For admissible data `D` the exponent `s` is `D.towerExp`, so that `D.E = P.E D.towerExp`.
* `P.Φ s` is the set of infinite places of `E`, a group isomorphic to `Gal(E/K)` by
  `P.galOfPlace s`; `Φ τ` is the complex embedding of `E` chosen at the infinite place `τ`.
* `finiteImage id y ∈ Ô E` says that `y` lies in the lattice `𝔞₀ = E ∩ α Ô`, where `α` is the idele
  of the Weil data and `Ô` is the ring of integral finite adeles.
* `P.periodFactor s` is a complex number; by `norm_iota_periodFactor` its absolute value at an
  embedding `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]` is given by the idele `α`.
* `β = (1 + √-d) / 2` is `quadGen d` in `ℂ`, `QuadField.betaK d` in `𝓞 K` and `P.betaKInE s` in
  `𝓞 E`.

In comments `P'(ζ)` is `P.relDifferentGen s`, the value at `ζ` of the derivative of the cyclotomic
polynomial of order `q₁`; `φ(q₁)` is the totient of `q₁`, `j` is the least integer with
`2 ^ j ≥ q₁`, and `y'† y = ∑ τ, τ(y) conj τ(y')`.

modules.title: Standard data as products of theta functions of the curve
modules.note:
* `New.IsTightFrame.isResolution`: a tight frame of length `b²` gives a resolution of the identity
  on `Eⁿ`.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_prod_twistedTranslate_eq_thetaProd_mul`: a product of translates of `θ` by
  `δ`-division points, taken at `δ̄ z`, is a power of a product of copies of `θ` times an integral
  series.
* `New.Parameters.exists_isVacuumExpansion`: the integral vacuum is an integral combination of
  translates of a vector whose theta function is a product of copies of `θ` along a tight frame;
  `New.Parameters.IsVacuumExpansion` collects the properties of this expansion.
* `New.Parameters.exists_jetSeries_map_eq_thetaProd_pow_mul`: the theta function of standard data of
  level `δ ≠ 0`, taken at `δ̄ (√(2π / √d) / Ω₀) z` with `d` and `Ω₀` as below, is the power `δ δ̄`
  of the product of `θ` along a resolution of the identity times an integral series in the
  parameters of these copies.

Standard data are integral combinations of translates of the integral vacuum. The proof has three
steps. Fourier inversion writes the integral vacuum through the translates of one product of copies
of `θ`, with a denominator prime to `p`. A translate of this product is a product of translates.
Each translated factor falls under the integrality principle on one curve.

Notions from other files:
* `finiteImage x` is the finite adelic vector `α⁻¹ x` of a rational vector `x`, where `α` is the
  idele of the Weil data of `E`; its coordinates lie in `Ô E` exactly when those of `x` lie in the
  lattice `𝔞₀ = E ∩ α Ô`.
* `V.ϱ (finVec x)` is the Heisenberg translation of `𝒮 V` by the finite adelic vector `α x`, called
  the translation by `x` below, and `V.finHeisenbergOp x` is this translation times a root of unity.
* `intVacuum V`, the integral vacuum, is the vacuum `V.vacElem` (a Gaussian times the signed
  indicator of the standard lattice) times a fixed power of the vacuum scale of the parameters.
* `daggerForms u` are the linear forms `u_j† z` read in `ℂ_p`, and `C.thetaProd μ m` is the product
  `∏ θ(μ_j z) ^ m j` of copies of the theta function of the curve `C`.
* `V.jetSeries c f` is the Taylor series of the theta function of `f` in Fock's coordinates, taken
  at `c z`. Here `P.areaScale` is the number `√(2π / √d)`, where `K = ℚ(√-d)`, and `P.cmPeriod` is
  the fixed period `Ω₀` of `K`: the lattice of the curve `P.cmCurve` is `Ω₀ 𝓞_K`. The factor
  `P.areaScale / P.cmPeriod` passes from Fock's coordinates to those of the curve
  `ℂ / cmPeriod 𝓞_K`.
* `finiteImage id a ∈ Ô E` says that the element `a` of `E` lies in `𝔞₀`; `Φ τ` is the complex
  embedding of the infinite place `τ` in the CM type.
* `IsTightFrame w m M` says that the `w i` lie in `𝔞₀` and that the matrix
  `(∑ m i τ(w i) conj σ(w i))`, indexed by infinite places `τ` and `σ`, is `M` times the identity.
  The number `M` is called the length of the frame.
* `V : Space E n ε` is a hermitian space of rank `n` with signs `ε` at the infinite places, together
  with an adelic point, `𝒮 V` is its Weil model, `V.θ` the theta functional on it, and
  `V.finitePart` the span of the images of the vacuum under the operators `V.finHeisenbergOp x`.
* `taylorVia ιₚ f` is the Taylor series of `f` at `0` read in `ℂ_p`, and `linearSeries μ` the linear
  form `μ` as a power series. `C.twistedTranslate k a f` is the translate of `f`, of weight `k`, by
  `a` times the factor that keeps it a theta function.

modules.title: Integrality and divisibility of the derivatives of standard data
modules.note:
This file bounds the valuations of the derivatives of the Taylor series of standard data along
homogeneous integral polynomials.

* Standard data of level `δ` at `p` (`standardData`): the span over the `p`-integral complex numbers
  (`embValRing`) of the translates of the integral vacuum by the points `x` for which `δ * x` is
  integral above `p`.
* `V.jetSeries a f`: the Taylor series at `0` of the theta function of `f`, with the variables
  scaled by `a`; the scale `P.jetScale s` is `periodFactor * areaScale / cmPeriod`.
* `jet R Q F`: the derivative `Q(∂) F` at `0`.
* The normal form (`HasNormalForm`): after scaling the variables by `ϖ`, an integral series times
  the exponential of a multiple of the coupling series of the pairs of partner places.
* `ιₚ`: the embedding of `ℂ` into `ℂ_[p]` that comes with `PadicPlace p`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Parameters.norm_jet_jetSeries_le_pow`: a lower bound for the valuations of the derivatives of
  the Taylor series of standard data along homogeneous integral polynomials.
* `New.Parameters.exists_hasNormalForm_jetSeries`: at a non-split prime the Taylor series of
  standard data of level one has the normal form.
* `New.Parameters.norm_jet_minorProd_jetSeries_le`: so its derivatives along products of minors have
  the predicted divisibility up to a loss of `card (P.Φ s) * N ^ 3 * (1 + Real.logb p (max (boxes κ
  N) 1))`, where `N = card n'`.
* `New.Parameters.norm_schurJet_jetSeries_le_of_charges`: the bound with removed columns and charges
  for the derivatives along the entries of the Schur matrices.

modules.title: Derivatives of integral expansions
modules.note:
* `New.exists_monomial_max_norm_coeff`: among the integral series in the `f i`, times a fixed
  series, a monomial of degree at most `|α|` has the largest coefficient at `α`.
* `New.CMLattice.katz_divisibility_limit`: for every `n` some `g ∈ 𝒪[[y]]` has `v(g⁽ⁿ⁾(0)) ≤ γ_p n`,
  where `γ_p = 1 / (p - 1) - ρ_p`.

The least valuation of `g⁽ⁿ⁾(0)` is superadditive in `n`, by the integrality of the group law, and
the formal parameter bounds it when `n` is a power of `q_p`. We work with absolute values, so that
least valuations become greatest norms and sums become products.

## Notation

* `d` is a prime congruent to `7` mod `8` (`PrimeSevenModEight d`), and a ring homomorphism
  `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]` is fixed (`PadicPlace p`).
* `C : CMLattice d` is a lattice `Λ` stable under the integers of `ℚ(√-d)`, with a point `t` of
  order two modulo `Λ` and a square root `a₁` of `12 ℘(t)`.
* `y = taylorVia ιₚ C.translatedY` is the Taylor series at `0` of
  `(℘'(z + t) - a₁ (℘(z + t) - ℘(t))) / 2`, carried to `ℂ_p` by the chosen map `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]`.
* `C.integralSeriesRing` is `𝒪[[y]]`, the power series in `y` over the valuation ring `𝒪` of `ℂ_p`.
* `primeNorm d p` is `q_p`, the norm of a prime of `ℚ(√-d)` above `p`, and `varpiValuation d p` is
  `ρ_p = 1 / (e (q_p - 1))`, with `e` the ramification index; `gammaPrime d p` is the rate
  `γ_p = 1 / (p - 1) - ρ_p`.
modules.literature: At inert primes the rate `γ_p` is that of Katz, Divisibilities, congruences, and Cartier duality.

modules.title: Least valuations of coefficients of theta products
modules.note:
The file bounds the least valuation `val_n(ν)` of a coefficient of degree `ν` in a product
`∏ (H_c Θ)(z_c)` over `n` copies of the variables.

The imported notions used in the statements are:

* `CMLattice d`: a lattice in `ℂ`, with a marked point `t` of order two and normalized at `t`, that
  is stable under the ring of integers of `ℚ(√-d)` if `d ≠ 0`. The results that need `d` to be a
  prime with `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)` assume `PrimeSevenModEight d`. Its function `C.θ` is the twisted
  translate by `t` of the sigma function with value `1` at `0`, and `C.translatedY` is an affine
  combination of `℘'(z + t)` and `℘(z + t)`.
* `PadicPlace p`: a ring homomorphism `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]`. By `taylorVia ιₚ f` is meant the Taylor
  series of `f` at `0` with `ιₚ` applied to the coefficients.
* `C.thetaProd μ m`: the series `Θ = ∏ θ(μ_j z) ^ m j`, where `θ` is the Taylor series of `C.θ`
  and the `μ_j` are linear forms over `ℂ_p`.
* `C.multiSeriesRing μ`: the ring of integral power series in the series `y(μ_j z)`, where `y` is
  the Taylor series of `C.translatedY`.
* `varpiValuation d p`: the number `ρ_p`, equal to `1 / (p - 1)`, `1 / (p² - 1)`, `1 / (2 p - 2)`
  when `p` is split, inert, ramified in `ℚ(√-d)`. A scaling of valuation at least `ρ_p` makes the
  series in `y` integral.
* `gammaPrime d p`: the rate `γ_p = 1 / (p - 1) - ρ_p`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.CMLattice.LeastValLE`: the relation `val_n(ν) ≤ r` for the least valuation of a coefficient
  of degree `ν` in a product `∏ (H_c Θ)(z_c)` over `n` copies of the variables.
* `New.CMLattice.LeastValLE.add`, `New.CMLattice.leastValLE_of_copySubst`: the two rules, for
  products and for integral substitutions.
* `New.CMLattice.scaledThetaProd`: the product `∏ Θ(δ_c z)` of scaled copies of `Θ`.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_scaledThetaProd_mem_mul_eq_one`: six scaled copies of `Θ` multiply to a unit
  of the ring of integral series in the `y(μ_j z)`.

modules.title: Least valuations along couplings
modules.note:
Throughout, `v` is the valuation of `ℂ_[p]` with `‖x‖ = p ^ (-v x)`, a series is integral if its
coefficients lie in the valuation ring `valRingCp p`, and `seriesToCp` views an integral series as a
series over `ℂ_[p]`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsCouplingFamily`: each selected coupling `z_τ ^ p ^ e τ * z_(τ⁺)` has `e τ` odd and has
  strictly the lowest exponent among such couplings of selected places with the same partner.
* `New.powerDegree`, `New.partnerDegree`: the degrees `ν'` and `ν''` of the two parts of a product
  of couplings, with their values at a place and their total degrees.
* `New.pairExponent`, `New.couplingSubst`: the exponent of `z' ^ ν' * z'' ^ ν''`, and the
  substitution `z_0 = δ_0 z' + z''`, `z_c = δ_c z'`.
* `New.IsCouplingFamily.norm_coeff_pairExponent`: the valuation of the coefficient of
  `z' ^ ν' * z'' ^ ν''` in `F(z' + z'') ∏_(c ≠ 0) F(δ_c z')` for `F = W exp (κ Ξ)`, where `κ` is a
  scalar of negative valuation.
* `New.CMLattice.leastValLE_six_of_isCouplingFamily`: at an inert prime `p > 2` the least valuation
  `val₆` on six copies satisfies `val₆(ν) ≤ -|j|` and `v(ν'! ν''!) + val₆(ν) ≤ γ_p |ν| - |j|`, where
  `ν = ν' + ν''` and `γ_p = gammaPrime d p = 1 / (p - 1) - varpiValuation d p`.

modules.title: Near pairs of `b`-places and the losses in the sharpness bound
modules.note:
This file studies places at a prime `p` that does not split in `K = ℚ(√-d)`, their partners, and the
`b`-places among them. A near pair is a `b`-place whose partner at an exponent `e < l₀ / 2` in `I_p`
is a `b`-place; `I_p` is the set of odd numbers, or of all `e ≥ 1` if `p = d`. For non-split `p ≤ k`
the `b`-places are sparse along the powers `(-p) ^ j` with `j < l₀`. For `p = d` there are no near
pairs. Writing `v` for the `p`-adic valuation, the file then bounds the losses in the sharpness
bound: for `p ≤ k` the terms of the sums `R_τ = D.partnerMinSum p τ` not coming from a near pair are
covered by `v(B)` for a product `B` of consecutive integers.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data P`: the data over the parameters `P = (q₀, d)`, with the size parameters `b`, `x`, `x₁`,
  `k`, the exponent `s` and the group `D.Φ` of infinite places of the field `E`.
* `l₀ = New.l₀ D.towerExp`: the least power of `3` above `27 s`, where `2 ^ s = m ^ 22`.
* `D.bPlaces`, `D.weight`: the set of `b`-places and the weight `κ` of a place, equal to `b` at the
  `b`-places and to `a / x₁` elsewhere, where `a = x b`.
* `D.placeOfInt ν`: the place named by the integer `ν`; the partner of `τ` at the exponent `e` is
  `P.partner D.towerExp p e τ = D.placeOfInt (-p ^ e) * τ`.
* `P.placeClass`: the class of a place modulo a divisor of `q₁ = towerDeg s * q₀`.
* `chiK d`: the character `χ_K = (· / d)`; `p` does not split in `K` if `χ_K(p) ≠ 1`.
* `positivePartnerExponents d p`, `piPrimeValuation d p`, `gammaPrime d p`: the set `I_p`, which is
  empty if `p` splits, and the numbers `v(π_p)` and `γ_p = v(π_p) ∑_{e ∈ I_p} p⁻ᵉ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.summable_posPart_sub_weight`: the series in the predicted valuation `S_p` converges.
* `New.Data.notMem_bPlaces_of_two_partners`: sparseness of the `b`-places along the powers of `-p`.
* `New.Data.IsNearPair.exponent_unique`, `New.Data.IsNearPair.eq_and_eq_of_partner_eq`,
  `New.Data.IsNearPair.end_ne_start`: for non-split `p ≤ k` no place occurs twice among the starts
  and ends of near pairs; two pairs that share a place contradict sparseness.
* `New.Data.lossProduct`: a product `B` of `n♯ = ⌈6 b / k⌉` consecutive integers, the last ones up
  to `l` if `n♯ ≤ l`, with `v(n♯!) ≤ v(B)` and `v(l!) ≤ v((l - n♯)₊!) + v(B)`.
* `New.Data.mul_sum_weight_sub_localPrimeSumTotal`: `γ_p |κ| - S_p = v(π_p) ∑ R_τ`, where `|κ|` is
  the sum of the weights.
* `New.Data.partnerMinSum_le`, `New.Data.error_le_padicValNat_lossProduct`: for `p ≤ k` the terms of
  `R_τ` other than that of a near pair are covered by `v(B)`.

modules.title: The valuation bound `v(l!) + val₁₂(l) ≤ S_p + 2 ∑ v(B_τ)` for every prime
modules.note:
Let `w` be a tight frame of length `M` with a linear form of unit coefficients, and let `val₆` and
`val₁₂` be the least valuations on six and twelve copies along `w`. This file proves the bound
`v(l!) + val₁₂(l) ≤ S_p + 2 ∑ v(B_τ)` for every prime `p` and every degree `l` near the weights,
that is, with `κ(τ) ≤ l_τ ≤ κ(τ) + x ^ 42` at all places `τ`. Here `v` is the `p`-adic valuation,
`l! = ∏ l_τ!`, and `x = D.x` is the length of the prime sum.

* `New.Parameters.resolutionForms`: the linear forms of a resolution, read in `ℂ_p`.
* `New.Data.isResolution_resolutionVectors`: a tight frame of length `M`, divided by an integer of

* `New.Data.leastValLE_six_zero_of_inert`: at an inert prime, `val₆(ν) ≤ 0` in all degrees.
* `New.Data.exists_hasNormalForm_resolutionForms`: at an inert prime the theta product along the
  frame has a normal form with unit leading coefficients.
* `New.Data.leastValLE_twelve`: `v(l!) + val₁₂(l) ≤ S_p + 2 ∑ v(B_τ)` for every prime `p`.

modules.note:
* `New.Data.exists_le_norm_coeff_indicatorDatum`: the reduction to the curve. Some Taylor
  coefficient of degree `l` of an indicator datum, times the factor `vacuumScale ^ 12` of the

  integral vacuum.

  factor `vacuumScale ^ 12` of the integral vacuum, has valuation at most `S_p + v(t)`.

modules.title: Galois conjugates of jets of theta functions and archimedean bounds for jets
modules.note:
An automorphism `σ` of `ℂ` over `K = ℚ(√-d)` acts on the jets of theta functions. This action is
realized as a `σ`-semilinear map `L` on `𝒮 V`, whose laws hold on `V.finitePart`. We then prove
archimedean bounds for the conjugates of the jets of admissible combinations of the operators
`New.Space.finHeisenbergOp` applied to the integral vacuum, moved by finite points of a pair of
groups.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Parameters.exists_isJetConjugation`: existence of `L`;
  `New.Parameters.IsJetConjugation.exists_map_schrodingerOp`: its action on the vacuum `vacElem` and
  on the data `Ψ ⊗ vacElem` for Schwartz–Bruhat functions `Ψ`;
  `New.Parameters.IsJetConjugation.norm_map_intVacuum_le`: a bound, with constant `P.constantBound`,
  for the images of the translates of `ω g (intVacuum V)`; it rests on
  `New.Parameters.norm_omega_vac_le`.
* `New.Parameters.norm_jet_le_of_isVacuumCombination` and
  `New.Parameters.sqrt_weylNormSq_schurJet_le_of_isVacuumCombination`: archimedean bounds for the
  conjugates by `σ ∈ Aut ℂ` of the jets, and for their Schur matrices;
  `New.Parameters.isVacuumCombination_of_isAdmissibleCombination` makes them apply to admissible
  combinations.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters.E`: The field `P.E s = K(ζ)`, for a primitive root of unity `ζ` of order
  `P.q₁ s`; `P.Φ s` is the set of its infinite places, a group isomorphic to `Gal(E/K)`.
* `New.Parameters.jetScale`: A nonzero complex number, the period factor times the area scale over
  the period `Ω₀`, at which Taylor series of theta functions are scaled.
* `New.Parameters.bigOmega`: The real number Ω = exp(γ − Re L′/L(1, χ_K))·2π/rd_E, with γ Euler's
  constant and rd_E the root discriminant of E.
* `New.Parameters.intVacuum`: The vacuum of rank n multiplied by the n-th power of a fixed number
  that makes its values at finite vectors integral.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.𝒮`: For a space V of rank n, a Banach space of integrable functions on 𝔸^n on which the
  Heisenberg and Weil representations act. Applied to an adelic vector, `f : 𝒮 V` gives the value
  of its theta function.

Related work: Bannai–Kobayashi, Algebraic theta functions and the p-adic interpolation of
Eisenstein–Kronecker numbers, 2010; Kings–Sprang, Eisenstein–Kronecker classes and integrality of
critical values, 2019; Katz, p-adic L-functions for CM fields, 1978.

representation is known; see `Lib.Weil.DualPair.KernelLaws` for sources.

modules.title: p-adic gauge bounds for one theta lift and data from functions modulo an ideal
modules.note:
This file derives `p`-adic bounds for one theta lift between the definite spaces with index types
`n` and `n'` from bounds on jets. A function `Ψ` on `n' × n` matrices modulo a modulus `𝔪`, put at
the places dividing `𝔪` with the integral vacuum elsewhere, gives a datum. If the values of `Ψ` are
integral away from `q`, an integer multiple of this datum is a standard datum at the primes not
dividing `q`.

* `New.Kernel.raises`: the additive monoid of data that multiply gauges by at most `max c 0`.

  with `d` diagonal at the places above `p` that define the gauge and `x`, `y` integral above `p`,
  raises gauges by at most `max B 0` for any bound `B` on the weighted entries of the jet matrices.
* `New.Parameters.mem_raises_of_standardData`: an explicit bound for a standard datum itself.
* `New.Parameters.smul_mem_raises_of_dvd`: if a multiple of a datum is standard and the scale is

* `New.Parameters.smul_vacuumDatum_mem_standardData`: if `q * N` lies in `𝔪` and the values of `Ψ`

* `New.Parameters.isVacuumCombination_vacuumDatum`: the datum is a combination of translates of the

modules.title: Inserting a block into a parameter
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
The parameters of all chains and grids of spaces are built in one way. There are a stem and a finite
set C of centres, each with a length and a kind, down or up. For B ⊆ C the vector λ⁺_B consists of
the stem and the blocks c + [l_c], c ∈ B, and the sign of an entry is −1 to the power of the number
of centres outside B that are down and above it or up and below it. The parameter λ_B is λ⁺_B
lowered by ½ or by 0, as the parity of the rank requires. Everything is at one infinite place, and
entries are doubled.

* `New.CentreSystem`, `New.CentreSystem.IsSeparated`, `New.CentreSystem.IsParam`: the data, the
  conditions on parities and distances, and the parameter λ_B on a space with these signs, up to a
  common sign σ.
* `New.CentreSystem.IsParam.isBlockRule_insert_of_down`,
  `New.CentreSystem.IsParam.isBlockRule_neg_insert_of_up`: the parameters before and after the
  insertion of a block correspond (`New.IsBlockRule`): the parameters themselves for a down centre,
  their negatives for an up centre.

* `HCParam s`: integer vectors l = 2λ indexed by the coordinates of a space with signs s.
* `HCParam.HasGap l h`: the entries of λ are distinct and lie in (n − 1)/2 + ℤ, n the rank, and

modules.title: Direct and mirror data modulo `N`, and the operator `Up`
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
Let `P` contain one place of each conjugate pair above the split prime `N` of the CM field `E`. A
marked lattice at `P` is a lattice `L` with a vector `ε` of `L / N L` that is non-zero at every
place. Everything here is written in a basis of `L` whose last vector lifts `ε`, at all places of
`P` at once:
* the stabiliser of `(L, ε)` is `mirabolic`, and `diagNInv` takes `L` to `L⁺ = L + 𝒪 ε / N`;
* the direct datum `1[S L ⊆ L', S ε = ε']` is `directDatum`; in bases of `L⁺` and `L'⁺` it is
  `lastRowDatum`;
* the mirror datum `1[S L ⊆ L'⁺] ψ_N (u' (S ε))`, where `u'` is the linear form on `L'⁺` with kernel
  `L'` and `u' (ε' / N) = 1`, is `mirrorDatum` in bases of `L` and `L'⁺`;
* the operator `Up`, which replaces `L` by `L⁺` and sums against `ψ_N` over the primitive vectors
  with unit last entry, is `upOperator`.

A `LiftLaw` records how a lift depends on its datum. On ramified vectors the following hold. A
mirror lift, moved by `diagNInv`, is `Up` after a direct lift, and `Up` moves through a direct lift
up to the factor `γ` of its law. A glued double lift is the number of primitive vectors times a
mirror lift after a direct lift; hence, moved by `diagNInv`, it is a scalar times two direct lifts
after `Up`. So a chain of glued double lifts is a scalar times a chain of direct lifts after a power
of `Up`.

Notions from other files:
* `FinPlace E` is the set of finite places of `E`, `star w` the conjugate place, `LocField w` the
  completion `E_w` with valuation `v` (integral means `v x ≤ 1`) and `ResField w` its residue field.
* `LocProd P` is the product of the `E_w` over `w ∈ P`, and `O` is its ring of integers.
* `stdLattice.selfDualAddChar E` is the additive character of the finite adeles `𝔸f E` fixed by the
  Weil data.
* `liftIntegralFn r f` is `S ↦ f (r S)` on integral matrices `S` and zero elsewhere.
* `compUpTo f j` is the composite `f (j - 1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ f 0` of a chain of linear maps.

modules.title: Descent pairs: descent data for theta lifts to definite unitary groups
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file sets up the theta lift from U(W), with W of rank r, to the definite group U(V), with
V = `New.stdSpace` of rank n > r, and the descent from V to W. One structure, `New.DescentPair`,
holds the data: the places of the level, the space W, an embedding of the indices of its basis into
those of V, a numbering of its basis vectors, the numbers of columns k⁺ and k⁻, and a character of
U(1)(𝔸) with its weight and tame part. The level sits at two finite families of split places
(`New.LevelPlaces`): M, the chosen places `chosenPlace`, and Q, the places `twistPlace` of the
twist. The residue field at w is k_w = `New.ResField w`. The finite datum Ψ_bl ⊗ vac is a vector of
the Weil representation `New.pairWeil` on `Hom(W, V)`: the block datum Ψ_bl, a function of the
reductions of a matrix at M and Q, with the vacuum at the other finite places.

For a descent pair `O`, the character of the descent datum is `O.u1Char`, with weight `O.weight` and
tame part `O.tamePart`. The highest weight of the forms on V is `(O.columnCount, O.detExp)`, given
by numbers of columns. Vectors of the representation of this weight are written ξ, and forms on V
are written Ξ.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DescentPair`: the data of a descent pair; `New.DescentPair.FormV`: its forms on V, with the
  action `New.DescentPair.formAction` of ∏_M GL_r and the Hecke polynomial
  `New.DescentPair.heckePolyOnForms`.
* `New.DescentPair.fockPoly`, `New.DescentPair.blockDatum`, `New.DescentPair.conjKernel`,
  `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent`: the Fock polynomial of a vector, the finite datum Ψ_bl ⊗ vac,
  the conjugate theta kernel as a linear form on weight vectors, and the normalized descent from
  forms on V to functions on U(W)(𝔸).
* `New.DescentPair.blockDatum_eq_sum_modDatum`: Ψ_bl ⊗ vac is the sum of the translates of Ψ¹ ⊗ vac,
  with Ψ¹ = `New.DescentPair.identityBlockIndicator`, by lifts (`New.LevelPlaces.twistResidueLift`)
  of the inverses of the elements of `∏ GL(k_w)` over `Q` (`New.LevelPlaces.TwistGL`).

  weight of forms on `V`.
* `New.DescentPair.FitsParams`: the data of a descent pair `O` are those of a parameter `l` on `W`
  and `l'` on `V`.
* `New.DescentPair.FitsParams.exists_isJointHarmonic`, `New.DescentPair.FitsParams.isEdge`: then the
  polynomial of the highest vector is a product of joint harmonics (staircases of minors), so it is
  an edge from `l` to `l'`.
* `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent_eq_smul_star_lift_swap`: the normalized descent
  `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent`, defined by a class sum, is a multiple of the descent by the
  datum of the highest vector, the conjugate of the transposed lift (`New.Space.lift` from `V` to
  `W`) of the conjugate form.

* `New.levelOf w H`: the subgroup of K₀ = `New.stdLevel` of the elements whose reductions at the
  places `w i` form an element of H.
* `New.levelSpace π K χ`: the vectors on which each k in K acts through π by the scalar χ(k).
* `New.HasHeckePolynomial π hw p y`: y is spherical at the split place w, and the Hecke polynomial

* `New.IsJointHarmonic`: a nonzero polynomial that is highest, of the lowest K-types, for the row
  and the column actions and harmonic in both directions.

modules.title: Good labels, index types of hermitian spaces, the group 𝖦 and idempotent e₀
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file introduces primitive polynomials and good tuples of labels at one prime. Then, for
admissible data D, it introduces the index types and signs for the bases of the hermitian spaces
X_j, Y_j and W_j.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsPrimitivePolynomial`: irreducible labels with a root of order |k|^r − 1. They are stable
  under scaling the roots by an M-th root of unity if M² ∣ |k| − 1
  (`New.IsPrimitivePolynomial.scaleRoots`). The product of their roots has order |k| − 1
  (`New.IsPrimitivePolynomial.isPrimitiveRoot_prod_aroots_and_exists_pow_eq`).
* `New.goodTuples`: tuples of labels, each without roots among the M-th roots of unity of its base
  field, of which at least one is primitive.
* `New.Data.X`, `New.Data.RowIndex`, `New.Data.Y`: the basis indices of X_j (rank `New.Data.n`), of
  Y_0 (rank r, `New.Data.card_rowIndex`) and of Y_j (`New.Data.RowIndex` and j blocks of size
  `New.Data.t`).
* `New.Data.chosenGL`, `New.Data.e₀`: the product of the groups GL_r over the residue fields at the
  chosen places above p₀, p₁, and the good idempotent in its group algebra. The idempotent is the
  sum of the idempotents `New.tupleIdem` over `New.Data.goodTupleFamilies`.
* `New.Data.isCentralProj_e₀`: `e₀` is a central idempotent.
* `New.Data.hyperplaneSum_mul_e₀`: `e₀` kills pure tensors with a factor `New.hyperplaneSum χ l`,
  `l ≠ 0`, `χ ^ q₂ = 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data`: the data D, with m lifts, block size t and ranks k, n_j = k + j (t + 1) and
  r = k + m − 1; s is its parameter `D.towerExp`, and q₂ = q₂(s) the integer `New.Parameters.q₂`.
* `New.Data.ChosenPlace`: the chosen places above the level prime p_i (i = 0, 1), the finite places
  of E that divide both p_i and the conjugate `D.piM` of an integer of K of norm p₀p₁.
* `New.IsLabel`: a label of degree r is a monic squarefree polynomial c of degree r with c(0) ≠ 0.
* `New.tupleIdem`: the tensor product of the label idempotents e_c of a tuple of polynomials.
* `New.piTensorElem`: the pure tensor ⊗ x_i in ℂ[∏ G_i] of elements x_i of ℂ[G_i].

modules.title: Harish-Chandra parameters, weights and lift diagrams of the definite spaces
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
A weight is given by its last entry and by the number of columns of each height of its Young diagram
at each infinite place of `E`. This file fixes the weights on the spaces `X_j` and `Y_m`. It defines
the Harish-Chandra parameters of the `X_j` and of `Y_m` in decreasing order, the highest weights
`μ(X_j)` and `μ(Y_m)`, and the diagrams of the lifts between the `X_j`. It computes the columns and
bounds the rows of these diagrams, and it shows that `μ(X_m)` and `μ(Y_m)` interlace. It also
computes `n_τ = |μ(X_m)_τ| - |μ(Y_m)_τ|`, where `|·|` is the sum of the entries.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.columnCount`, `New.Data.lastEntry`: the columns and the last entry of the weight on
  `X_j`.
* `New.Data.keptColumns`, `New.Data.columnsY`: the columns of the weight on `Y_m`, obtained by
  branching.
* `New.Data.paramX`, `New.Data.weightX`, `New.Data.liftDiagram`: the doubled parameters and the
  weights of the `X_j`, and the diagrams of the lifts.
* `New.Data.weightX_eq`, `New.Data.weightY_eq`: the weights in terms of their columns.
* `New.Data.branchExponent_eq`: the formula for `n_τ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data`: data `D` for parameters `P : New.Parameters`. They give a CM field `E`, the number
  `m = D.m` of lifts and a rank `r = D.r`. From these come `k = D.k = r + 1 - m`, `t = D.t = 5 r`,
  the ranks `n_j = D.n j = k + j (t + 1)` and the gap `Δ = D.gap = 2 * D.halfGap = 2 r ^ 8`.
* `X_j`, `Y_m`: the standard definite hermitian spaces over `E` of ranks `n_j` and `n_m - 1`. Lift
  `j + 1` is the theta lift from forms on `U(X_j)` to forms on `U(X_{j+1})`. Branching is the
  restriction of representations from `U(X_m)` to `U(Y_m)`. This file has only their weights.
* `New.Data.Φ`: the set of infinite places of `E`.
* `New.Data.a`, `New.Data.aPlaces`: the integer `a = x b`, for the scales `x` and `b` of the data,
  and the set of `a`-places, the places `≡ 1` modulo `P.q₀`.
* `New.Data.liftWeight`: the weight `κ_j(σ) = κ(σ) + (j + 1/2) Δ` at `σ`, with `κ = D.weight`. It is
  not to be confused with the column count `New.Data.columnCount`.
* `New.Data.targetParameter`: the sequence `λ^Y = (k/2 - 1, …, 1 - k/2; -κ_{1/2}, -κ_{3/2}, …)` at a
  place, where `κ_{i - 1/2} = κ_i - Δ / 2`.

modules.title: Chains of theta lifts, jointly invariant combinations, and free levels
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file treats chains of theta lifts and their jointly invariant combinations for a general
tower of finite adelic unitary groups joined by theta kernels. It shows that, in bounded rank, the
levels that reduce to `1` at the chosen places are free, that is, that they have trivial
stabilisers `New.classAut`. The chosen places of `E = D.E` are the prime divisors of
`New.Data.piM`; `D.f` is the number of infinite places of `E`. For every integral level in bounded
rank, the orders of the stabilisers divide `New.Data.chosenGroupOrder`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.chain`: the composite of the first `j` lifts. It is equivariant (`New.chain_equivariant`),
  and its values are linear in the pure tensor of the data
  (`New.exists_linearMap_chain_eq_apply_pure`).
* `New.IsJointlyInvariant.sum_chain_mem_nsmul`: at free levels, a jointly invariant combination of
  chains is a sum with one term for each tuple of double cosets, with no denominators.
* `New.Data.principalLevel_le_chosenLevel`, `New.Data.classAut_eq_bot_of_le_chosenLevel`: in bounded
  rank, levels that reduce to `1` at the chosen places are free.
* `New.Data.card_classAut_dvd_chosenGroupOrder`: in rank at most `2 * D.n D.m` and for every
  integral level the stabilisers have order dividing `chosenGroupOrder`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.TensorChain`: The complex tensor product S_{j−1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ S_0, equal to ℂ for j = 0.
* `New.classAut`: `classAut Γ K g` is Γ ∩ gKg⁻¹, the stabiliser in Γ of the coset gK; here
  Γ = `stdRatPoints` is the rational unitary group of the standard definite space `New.stdSpace`,
  inside the finite adelic group.
* `New.Data.n`: The rank 𝗇_j = k + j(t + 1) of X_j.

modules.title: Index sets, signs and parameters of the grids; the parameters of every step correspond
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
Two grids of unitary groups, `Y` and `Ỹ`, with nodes `(i, j)`, are treated together by a flag `z`
(`false` for `Y`, `true` for `Ỹ`). A node has a base block of `r` (in `Ỹ`, `r + 1`) indices, `i`
added blocks of one kind and `j` of another (`New.BlockIndex`). For `z = false` the node `(i, j)` is
`Y^i_j` with its parameter. For `z = true` it is `Ỹ^j_i` with the negative of its parameter, so that
one formula serves both grids. An offset `o` shifts the second kind of block; the grids have
`o = 0`, and the nodes with `i = 0` are the intervals `[o + 1, o + j]` of the triangles.

* `New.Data.GridIndex`, `New.Data.gridSigns`, `New.Data.gridParam`: index set, signs and doubled
  parameter of a node.
* `New.Data.gridDiagEquiv`: at `(j, j)`, `j ≤ m`, `Ỹ` is `Y` plus one vector of sign `(-1)^j`.
* `New.Data.gridParam_interlace`: at the node `(m, m)` the parameter of `Y` and that of `Ỹ`
  (`-gridParam true`) interlace.
* `New.Data.gridCentres`, `New.Data.isParam_gridParam`: the parameter of a node consists of a stem
  and the blocks of a set of centres (`New.CentreSystem`).
* `New.Data.paramsCorrespond_grid_succ_left`, `New.Data.paramsCorrespond_grid_succ_right`,
  `New.Data.paramsCorrespond_leftPair`: each step inserts a block, so the parameters correspond
  (`New.ParamsCorrespond`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data`: the admissible data `D`, with `m` (even) lifts, the rank `r` (odd), `k = r + 1 - m`,
  `t = 5 r`, the gap `Δ = D.gap = 2 halfGap` and the set `D.Φ` of infinite places.
* `New.Data.RowIndex`: an index set with `r` elements, numbered by `New.Data.basisNumber`.
* `New.Data.liftWeight`: the centre `w_j = κ_j = κ + (j + 1/2) Δ` at an infinite place, with
  `κ = D.weight`, the gap `Δ = D.gap` and `Δ / 2 = D.halfGap`.
* `New.Data.targetParameter`: the target parameter, the vector
  `λ^Y = ([k - 1]; -κ_{1/2}, -κ_{3/2}, …)`, with entries numbered from `0`; the entry `r` is
  `-κ_{m+1/2}`.
* `New.ParamsCorrespond γ γ' l l' s s'`: at each infinite place, the doubled parameters `l` (signs
  `s`) and `l'` (signs `s'`) satisfy the block rule (`New.IsBlockRule`) for the weights `γ`, `γ'`.

modules.title: Levels of the chain, chain data, and the composite lift
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
The map `New.Data.compositeLift` on source forms is built from chains of `m` theta lifts
`X_0 → X_1 → ⋯ → X_m` between definite unitary groups, followed by restriction to the block `Y_m` of
one rank less. Here `X_j` is an index set of `𝗇_j = k + j(t + 1)` elements. The weight at stage `j`
is given by the column numbers `New.Data.columnCount` and the determinant exponents
`New.Data.lastEntry`. This file defines the levels and spaces of forms of the stages, the
restriction from `X_m` to `Y_m`, the kernels of the lifts, the glued datum at `N` in the
Schrödinger model, and chain data.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.restrictedChain`: ∑_x Ψ(x) · (chain with the data of x), then `New.Data.restrictToY`.
* `New.Data.IsChainDatum`, `New.Data.compositeLift`: chain data, and the same map for the data glued
  above `N` in each double lift.

Notions from other files:
* `New.classAut`: `classAut Γ K g` is Γ ∩ gKg⁻¹, the stabiliser in Γ of the coset gK; here
  Γ = `stdRatPoints` is the rational unitary group of the standard definite space `New.stdSpace`,
  inside the finite adelic group.
* `New.Data.n`: The rank 𝗇_j = k + j(t + 1) of X_j.
* `New.Data.columnCount`: The number of columns of height h < 𝗇_j at the infinite place τ in the
  weight on X_j; it does not depend on j. For h = 1 it is `D.a` at the places in `New.Data.aPlaces`
  and 0 elsewhere; for h = k ≠ 1 it is κ_1(τ) − ⌊𝗇_1 / 2⌋, with κ_j = `D.liftWeight j`; for h > k
  with h ≡ k mod t + 1 it is `D.gap` − (t + 1); otherwise it is 0.
* `New.chain` (in `New.UpperBound.Objects.LiftChains`): the composite of the first `j` theta lifts.
* `New.Data.chosenLevel` (in `New.UpperBound.Objects.LiftChains`): the integral elements that
  reduce to `1` at every chosen place, that is, at every prime divisor of `D.piM`.
modules.literature:
This file sets up the objects of the upper bound. Related work is listed with the results on them,
in `New.UpperBound.Divisibility.LocalDivisibility`, `New.UpperBound.Seesaw.SeesawIdentity` and
